top.title: ACAMB advises bank customers against phishing scams
top.description: The Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has urged bank customers to remain vigilant against phishing scams and other forms of cyber fraud, warning that criminals are increasingly using fake bank alerts, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal sensitive financial information. The warning follows a fraudulent text message impersonating various banks. FactCheckAfrica debunked the message, finding that the link it contained led to a cloned internet banking website designed to steal customers’ login credentials, BVNs, card details and transaction PINs. The incident highlights the risks associated with digital banking fraud in Nigeria. In June, Wema Bank suspended its engagements on X, (formerly known as Twitter) amid reports of more than 70 fake accounts impersonating the bank and its ALAT platform. In August, Zenith Bank Plc disclosed that it was investigating unauthorised access to customer data linked to a global cyberattack. ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, warned that fraudsters were increasingly adopting sophisticated methods to impersonate trusted banking brands and steal customers’ personal information, making their schemes difficult to distinguish from legitimate communications. “When a scam message carries your name, your phone number or your bank’s logo, it looks real. That is exactly why customers must slow down. No bank in Nigeria will ask you to confirm your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link,” Sipe said. Sipe acknowledged the efforts of banks to strengthen fraud detection and customer protection, alongside regulatory measures introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s mandatory cybersecurity self assessment guide. He stressed, however, that these efforts must be complemented by customer awareness and vigilance, particularly when handling requests for sensitive banking information. “Banks can strengthen their security systems, but fraudsters continue to find ways to exploit unsuspecting customers. We must all remain vigilant. Always pause, verify requests through official channels and report anything suspicious before taking action,” he added. Sipe urged customers to avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages asking them to verify, reactivate or secure their bank accounts. He also warned against sharing personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), card verification values (CVVs) or BVNs in response to suspicious requests. Customers should verify such requests directly with their banks through official mobile applications, verified social media accounts or published customer service numbers. top.title: World Ports Confab: FG woos global investors with maritime reforms
top.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has intensified efforts to attract global investment into Nigeria’s maritime sector by showcasing the Federal Government’s ongoing port reforms and investor-friendly policies at the World Ports Conference, highlighting opportunities for private sector participation, improved port efficiency and sustainable growth. Speaking at the ongoing World Ports Conference in London, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, showcased President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s maritime policies and its positioning of Nigeria’s Ports as Africa’s biggest economy that is yearning for global investment. He affirmed that the speed of growth and development in the country’s ports signifies the huge opportunities investors should tap into, adding that the current administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has put policies in place that are investment friendly. The NPA boss identified Nigeria’s huge population, urbanization, and infrastructural gaps in the ports as attractive opportunities for investment in its maritime and associated sectors. Dantsoho, who is also the Vice- President of the International Association of Ports & Harbours (IAPH) and doubles as Chairman of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA) told investors that Africa’s untapped resources remain the best destination for ports investment and development. He said the government alone cannot fund development of bigger or deeper sea ports and other similar projects hence the need for investors to take advantage of such opportunities across the continent. Dantsoho affirmed that “Nigeria has the highest population in Africa. So, the speed of growth is something that really should concern us. For example, in Nigeria, only recently, about 3 years ago, we commissioned the first deep sea port in Nigeria, which is called Lekki Deep Sea Port, that was funded by the Chinese government in relationship with China Harbor, and the expenditure cost us $1.6 billion to build Lekki in Lagos. top.title: BoI advocates investment in industrial clusters to boost Lagos economy
top.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Bank of Industry (BOI) has called for increased investment in industrial clusters, reliable power supply and supporting infrastructure to boost productivity, attract private capital and strengthen the Lagos State economy. Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, BoI, Dr. Olasupo Olusi made this call in a keynote address delivered at the 4th edition of the Lagos Economic Outlook 2027 Discourse, themed, ‘“Development Pathways, Emerging Risks and Strategic Policy Priorities.’ Represented by Dr. Isa Omagu, General Manager, MD/CEO’s Office, BoI, Olusi said investment in industrial clusters, particularly along major industrial and port corridors, would help businesses overcome production constraints, reduce operating costs and improve their competitiveness. He also said Lagos must assess economic progress by the improvements businesses and residents experience, rather than relying solely on economic growth figures and public spending. “The test is whether Lagos becomes more productive and more liveable,” he said. He identified electricity costs, traffic congestion, access to appropriate financing and institutional coordination as major constraints to business productivity. “A manufacturer needs reliable electricity. A worker needs a commute that does not consume productive hours. Firms need predictable approvals, appropriate finance and customers,” he said. Olusi urged the state to prioritise investment in power infrastructure serving industrial clusters, faster freight movement, streamlined business approvals, flood-resilient commercial routes and skills development. Speaking at the event, Lagos State Commissioner for Economic Planning and Budget, Mr. Ope George, said the ministry would continue to coordinate economic intelligence, development planning, budget management and performance monitoring in support of Lagos State’s long-term development aspirations. He said the 2027 economic outlook provided an opportunity to consolidate the state’s achievements, address structural challenges and strengthen its position as a competitive and resilient economy. “Our focus goes beyond economic projections. It is about shaping policies that will strengthen competitiveness, promote inclusive growth and secure a sustainable future for Lagos State,” George said. Earlier, Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget, Mrs. Olayinka Ojo, highlighted the state’s development planning, budget monitoring and performance evaluation frameworks. She said Lagos was strengthening evidence-based governance through its long-term development plan, Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, annual budgets and regular monitoring of revenue, expenditure and project delivery. Ojo also highlighted the government’s engagement with communities and the use of platforms to improve citizens’ access to information on public projects and social intervention programmes. top.title: 'I'm so tired and also disappointed' - Matheus Cunha admits sitting in the relegation zone 'is not normal' after Manchester United's 4-4 thriller against Aston Villa
top.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United forward Matheus Cunha has expressed his exhaustion and frustration after his side twice fought back from two goals down to salvage a 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa. Despite rescuing a dramatic late point at Old Trafford on Sunday, the Red Devils enter the November international break languishing in 18th place. Brazilian forward laments slow starts Cunha played the full 90 minutes on Sunday after inspiring a midweek 3-2 Champions League comeback win over Roma , earning a 16th-minute penalty when fouled by Boubacar Kamara and testing keeper Zion Suzuki from distance. Bruno Fernandes converted that spot-kick before Youri Tielemans cancelled out early strikes from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson. After John McGinn's penalty and Leon Goretzka made it 4-2, stoppage-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point . Late comebacks mask mentality issue Questioning why his team only show urgency after falling behind, Cunha told Sky Sports : "I'm so tired and also disappointed. After the other night [against Roma] we talked about how we concede goals and have the mentality to come back in the game. "We did it again where we had to play like Manchester United and go forward. We showed courage, but we only do this after we concede goals. "We showed character after conceding goals. If we had shown that character and courage before, then we will win more games. "I don't know why we are making it hard for ourselves. We all work hard, and we all want to be the best. We need to change our mentality from the beginning." Attacker sympathises with frustrated supporters Failing to keep a clean sheet across their opening 10 league games for the first time since 1986-87 has left United in their lowest position at this stage of a top-flight campaign since sitting 20th that same season. Understanding why the Old Trafford faithful are unhappy , Cunha added: "Before we played, everyone is a fan. You understand why they are frustrated. This is completely fine; we understand. "We are on the pitch, and we need to manage this. We need to change the mentality, be in the game. I don't think the fans are against us; it's just that they want to see us perform and win games. "Before anything else, we need to look inside to us - the players, the staff. It's a huge club and to feel something like this [being so low down in the standings] is not normal." Liverpool test awaits after hiatus Winless in eight Premier League outings to match a barren run from April to May 2025, United are now guaranteed to spend at least 15 straight days in the drop zone , their longest top-flight stretch since a 28-day spell in September and October 1986. Cunha and his team-mates must use the two-week international pause to fix their defensive flaws. Once domestic action resumes in a fortnight, the Red Devils face a daunting clash against rivals Liverpool.

top.title: MVPW07 Results: Baumgardner Defuses Turhan, Unification Fight Looming
top.description: What to Know Women’s boxing thrilled fans in Arlington, Texas and watching on ESPN at Most Valuable Promotions’ MVPW07 card on Sunday. Alycia Baumgardner took Elif Nur Turhan to the cleaners with three shutout scorecards in a dominating performance. Ramla Ali scored her biggest, while Irma Garcia and Skye Nicolson defended their titles. In Sunday’s main event on the Most Valuable Promotions MVPW07 card, Alycia Baumgardner of Detroit stepped up and showed out in her first fight as a lightweight. Alycia Baumgardner reacts to her three shutout scorecards declaring her the winner. Photo: Most Valuable Promotions “The Bomb” thoroughly defused one of boxing’s hard-punching women and our 2025 Fighter of the Year , Elif Nur Turhan of Turkey. Turhan did not win a single round on any of the three scorecards against Baumgardner, a triple 100-90 shutout. Baumgardner is now the IBF World Lightweight champion. It was the first loss for “The Golden Turkish Warrior” Turhan (14-1, 8 KOs) at the hands of Baumgardner (19-1, 7 KOs ), who has never looked more in control. “This was somebody that I was very humble to fight, and I needed this fight to keep me humble, to keep me hungry, and be the best fighter that I can be,” said Baumgardner. Baumgardner and trainer Derrick James trained hard and put together the ideal game plan against Turhan. Turhan swings for the fences, relying on her power much like a male heavyweight who can lose every round but win the fight with a single punch. They recognized that Baumgardner could neutralize her with speed, with a stinging jab and straight power shots. Baumgardner said she and James knew Turhan would come out swinging. “ We knew that’s how she comes to fight. So it was all about staying composed and staying true to what I’m great at, and that’s keeping my hands up. That’s being skillful. The skills pay the bills, baby!” Baumgardner landed more than half of her power punches thanks to her superior accuracy and counterpunching. She was well conditioned to fight three-minute rounds, saying she sparred more than 160 rounds in training camp. It paid off: her punch output increased through the fight, and she threw and landed the most punches in the final round as Turhan faded. According to CompuBox, Turhan landed an average of just five punches per round. Baumgardner landed 43% of her punches thrown in combination to just 16% for Turhan. “I was prepared for that fight, and so when I’m in there, I just think, man, I trained for this,” said Baumgardner. “This was supposed to be the fun part, and I definitely made it fun and made it exciting and entertaining, and I hope everybody was entertained tonight.” Sitting ringside watching with great interest was WBC/WBO World Lightweight champion Caroline Dubois, who will face WBA World Lightweight champion Stephanie Han to unify the rest of the titles on February 20 in El Paso . Count on a fight for undisputed between the winner and Baumgardner in the spring. Ramla Ali Wins First World Title

top.title: Footballer to help kids get their kicks outdoor
top.description: Hull City captain Lewie Coyle is encouraging children to play with a smile [Jasmine Lowe/BBC News] The captain of a Premier League team has launched a street football programme to encourage more children to enjoy outdoor play. Hull City defender Lewie Coyle said his career began by kicking a ball in an alleyway near the East Hull home where he grew up and he has called for more children to follow in his footsteps. The 31-year-old said: "I believe being allowed to lark (play) about outside gave me a head start in pursuing what my career has turned out to be as a professional footballer." Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, is backing Coyle's call: "Playing outside develops confidence, creativity, resilience and independence. It's good for physical and mental health." Coyle led his hometown club to victory in the Championship play-off final in May, securing the Tigers' promotion to the Premier League. Through the Lewie Coyle Football Academy, the defender is launching LCFA Street Football and has vowed to visit estates across the city and hold free pop-up events to encourage outdoor play among children. Coyle said his Hull City team-mates had donated as part of the campaign to ensure every child taking part received a free football. He said: "I just want to encourage kids to move again. We need kids to be kids and play on the street, but of course, in a safe environment. "I had so many amazing memories growing up on the streets of Bilton. It taught me confidence and social skills, and it was character-building. "We're in an era now where kids socialise through technology, but I think as adults we need to make sure there's more of a push for our children to play out in the same way we did. "We're going to chuck some jumpers down and use them as goalposts, and we're really going to throw it back. As it says on the tin, we're just going to have a kickabout on the streets." Scunthorpe-born Dame Rachel de Souza is backing Lewie Coyle's call for more outdoor play [PA Media] Coyle's message has been backed by de Souza, who said it echoed new research from her office that showed "boys and girls want to play outside". She said: "I've spoken to children across the nation through my Big Future survey and, from Land's End to Hadrian's Wall, I hear the same message: boys and girls want to play. "They want to be outside, be active and be with friends in places where they feel safe and welcome. "But, there are so many barriers right now, from the cost of living to a lack of places to go, especially for teenagers and disabled children. "We all need to champion play and remember that childhood can't be, and shouldn't be, completely risk-free." top.title: Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years
top.description: •Cargoes to ease pressure on substations, strengthen national grid — Tegbe By Udeme Akpan The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has released 98 containers of electricity transmission equipment stranded at the nation’s ports, some for up to 20 years, in a move expected to strengthen the national grid and improve electricity supply across the country. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this in Lagos, stating that 44 containers were released from ENL Terminal, while another 54 were cleared from APMT and Sun & Moon Terminals. He said the 98 containers represented part of more than 300 containers of transmission equipment held at the ports. The equipment, comprising high-capacity transformers, cables and switchgear, was procured to expand the transmission network, address overloaded substations and improve electricity delivery nationwide. Tegbe said: “The equipment was procured to expand the transmission network and relieve overloaded substations. Its detention stalled projects, kept existing substations under heavy strain, exposed valuable assets to deterioration and accumulated charges on the cargoes.” He noted that the prolonged detention of the equipment had imposed additional costs on businesses, households and public institutions, which continued to grapple with unreliable electricity supply. Also speaking, the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adeniyi, said the Service had commenced processes to clear the containers in collaboration with the Ministry of Power, the Nigerian Ports Authority and terminal operators. He said: “The release follows the President’s directive for immediate clearance and for agencies to resolve outstanding charges and administrative bottlenecks without delay.” Adeniyi pledged to work with the Minister until all the containers were cleared, while appealing to terminal operators to support the national effort. The Minister disclosed that an inspection of the recovered equipment showed that most of the items remained useful and viable. He said: “When evacuated, it will be verified, tested and refurbished where necessary, then deployed to project sites to complete stalled installations, relieve overloaded substations and strengthen constrained transmission corridors.” The post Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: COP31 Opens As Climate, Geopolitical Pressures Mount
top.description: The UN’s annual climate talks kick off Monday in Turkey as rising temperatures heighten the urgency of action, with financial constraints and geopolitical tensions complicating efforts to secure global cooperation. More than 100,000 people are expected to attend COP31 in a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean seaside city of Antalya over the next two weeks. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are facing tough discussions over how to accelerate the energy transition and provide funds to help developing nations cope with the worsening climate emergency. But observers say few major breakthroughs are expected as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The climate emergency, meanwhile, continued to wreak havoc this year as punishing heatwaves baked Europe, wildfires raged in Indonesia, and a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods in Nepal. An exceptionally strong El Niño climate phenomenon is forecast to peak later this year, adding to extreme weather and possibly helping to make 2026 or 2027 the hottest year on record. The outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above preindustrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. “Global leaders must pull us back from the brink and commit to rapidly transitioning away from fossil fuels and expanding renewable energy, an imperative reinforced by the current energy affordability crisis,” said Rachel Cleetus, climate programme director at the Union of Concerned Scientists. A woman walks inside the COP31 venue at the Antalya Expo Center on November 8, 2026, ahead of the opening of the UN climate conference. ‘Clean’ Electrification? Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference. The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements. Turkey is promoting an “action agenda” alongside the formal negotiations that encourages countries to support non-binding pledges on issues from artificial intelligence to waste management. Its centrepiece is an “electrification” drive to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035. But the initiative could become a source of friction. The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of fossil fuels in the Turkish proposal. Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action. top.title: Matchday Musings: Sunderland Return To Winning Ways Against Chelsea
top.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Mike Penders of Chelsea fails to save a penalty from Enzo Le Fee of Sunderland as he scores his team’s first goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Chelsea FC at Stadium of Light on November 08, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images One word to describe this: massive. It felt that way inside the stadium before the game, and it felt like it at full time as Sunderland ran out 1-0 winners against Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea thanks to Enzo Le Fée’s first half penalty. Regis Le Bris made seven changes from the team that lost to Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday, with Thomas Meunier, Nordi Mukiele, Luke O’Nien, Reinildo Mandava, Le Fée, Chemsdine Talbi and Brian Brobbey coming into the starting eleven. A further change was enforced just two minutes in as Granit Xhaka went down injured and was replaced by Jules Ahoka. Sunderland started brightly, looking to take the game to Chelsea, pressing and harrying the Blues whenever they tried to play out from the back. Brobbey gave Levi Colwill a torrid time in the first half, constantly getting in behind the defender or holding him off to bring others in to play. Talbi ran at Marco Palestra time and time again, giving the Lads something we’ve desperately missed so far this season, and hopefully whatever happened between Talbi and Le Bris is done and dusted and we now start to see the Moroccan more consistently in the Premier League. There was a scare early on in the first half as a Chelsea appeal for a penalty was checked for what felt like an eternity by VAR. It did look like a foul by O’Nien on Cole Palmer but luckily the VAR decided the incident occurred outside the box, and there’ll be no arguments from anyone of a Sunderland persuasion, although I would imagine the majority were in shock that Jarred Gillett gave the decision our way — and those that were would’ve been even more shocked when he pointed to the spot at the other end after Colwill pulled and tripped Brobbey in the box. top.title: Michael Carrick sack update: INEOS to hold crunch talks at Carrington to decide Man United head coach’s fate
top.description: Michael Carrick sack update: INEOS to hold crunch talks at Carrington to decide Man United head coach’s fate INEOS had given Michael Carrick three games to save his job. Manchester United won only one of them. However, there were promising signs nonetheless. The Red Devils were the better team in the first half against Chelsea before Lisandro Martinez threw it all away in the second 45 minutes. top.title: OTD (09/11/1992): Crosby Is Caretaker At Sunderland… Again!
top.description: Sunderland 1-2 Leicester, League match at Roker Park, Sunday 15th November 1992. Brian Atkinson, Sunderland, gets the better of Colin Hull of Leicester. (Photo by NCJ Archive/Mirrorpix/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just six months earlier, it was probably the proudest moment in Malcolm Crosby’s footballing career as he led Sunderland out at Wembley as the manager who had taken them to the final and was ninety minutes away from becoming immortal. It wasn’t to be, as Liverpool ran out comfortable winners on the day, but then the real work was to begin. First up, his captain Paul Bracewell was fobbed off by the Sunderland board, so joined Keegan’s revolution up the road. Then Paul Hardyman had a tantrum because he was left out of the FA Cup final squad and joined Bristol Rovers. It was compounded by the fact that, after a whole host of players were linked with joining the club, only three signed to join the ranks. Shaun Cunnington from Grimsby Town, John Colquhoun from Hearts and, at weekends, Crosby’s assistant Bobby Ferguson called up his mate Terry Butcher to help us out, as his knee wouldn’t allow him to train. Things weren’t looking good to begin with, but four wins in the first 14 games confirmed everyone’s fears. It would be another season of struggle in Barclays League Division One (the Championship in new money). Two days earlier, Crosby’s Sunderland had been demolished 5-2 at Chris Turner’s Peterborough United, with the home side being 4-1 up on the hour mark. With the form the way it was, the table was looking bleak and, after a capitulation at London Road, it was looking like the end for Crosby as Sunderland manager. However, two days later, it was reported by Geoff Storey in the Sunderland Echo that Crosby would indeed be in the dugout for the next fixture at Roker Park against Leicester City. This wasn’t because the Roker boss had received a vote of confidence. It was reported “that the board had not been able to come up with a replacement that would appease disgruntled fans”. This led to comments by Aidan Semmens in the Echo, stating: “Malcolm Crosby began his career as Sunderland manager as caretaker. Now it seems he is in a caretaker’s role again”. There had been no word from chairman Bob Murray or the directors on the manager’s position, so much so that publicly Crosby believed his job was not under immediate threat: Everybody keeps going on about it, saying the board will sack me. The board has been great. They have let me get on with the job, but unfortunately we haven’t backed it up with results. Whatever decisions people make I, as a manager, have got to accept that decision. If they say enough is enough, I will have to accept that. Everybody knows that when you become a manager. I’m not worried about being sacked. What worries me is how we can play well in the two previous matches and at times play well against Peterborough, but then let goals in like we have. I’m worried about the players and I’m concerned for the supporters.

top.title: Lakers hold off Pistons behind Austin Reaves’ 43 with Luka Dončić out
top.description: Nov 8, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves (15) passes the ball from under the basket against the Detroit Pistons in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. DETROIT — The Lakers had led by 26. By the fourth quarter, that lead was down to one, and the NBA’s leading scorer was on the bench in street clothes. Austin Reaves took it from there. He hit an off-balance 3-pointer with 46 seconds left, waved toward the courtside seats and closed out a season-high 43-point night at the free-throw line as the Lakers beat the Detroit Pistons 121-116 on Sunday at Little Caesars Arena. The Lakers improved to 9-2 with their fifth straight win and are 2-0 without Luka Dončić, who missed his second game of the season with lower back tightness. Reaves went 14 of 27 from the field, made four of six 3-pointers and hit all 11 free throws. He added five rebounds and four assists and committed just one turnover against the NBA’s top-ranked defense. “I thought AR’s decision-making, his aggression, his ability to just consistently touch the paint and get downhill was fantastic tonight,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Quentin Grimes scored 10 of his 12 points in the first quarter, when L.A. shot 16 of 23 and built a 38-14 lead. The Lakers stretched it to 40-14 early in the second before Detroit’s bench brought the Pistons back. Daniss Jenkins scored 22 of his career-high 31 points in the first half, including a 3-pointer at the buzzer that cut the deficit to 61-48. Reaves scored 13 in the third quarter, but Detroit closed within three late in the period. The Pistons had a chance to tie it with 9:14 left in the fourth, when Cade Cunningham missed the second of two free throws to leave L.A. ahead 90-89. “We just stayed calm,” Reaves told Spectrum SportsNet. “You can get sped up in those types of moments, but we trust what we got on this team.” Walker Kessler helped rebuild the lead with a huge putback and a free throw to give L.A. an eight point lead with 2:15 left. He finished with 12 points, 16 rebounds and three blocks, while Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams each scored 17 off the bench. Kevin Huerter added 24 for Detroit, and Cunningham finished with 14 points and eight assists. The Lakers visit the Atlanta Hawks on Monday to close out the back-to-back.

nigeria.title: ACAMB advises bank customers against phishing scams
nigeria.description: The Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has urged bank customers to remain vigilant against phishing scams and other forms of cyber fraud, warning that criminals are increasingly using fake bank alerts, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal sensitive financial information. The warning follows a fraudulent text message impersonating various banks. FactCheckAfrica debunked the message, finding that the link it contained led to a cloned internet banking website designed to steal customers’ login credentials, BVNs, card details and transaction PINs. The incident highlights the risks associated with digital banking fraud in Nigeria. In June, Wema Bank suspended its engagements on X, (formerly known as Twitter) amid reports of more than 70 fake accounts impersonating the bank and its ALAT platform. In August, Zenith Bank Plc disclosed that it was investigating unauthorised access to customer data linked to a global cyberattack. ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, warned that fraudsters were increasingly adopting sophisticated methods to impersonate trusted banking brands and steal customers’ personal information, making their schemes difficult to distinguish from legitimate communications. “When a scam message carries your name, your phone number or your bank’s logo, it looks real. That is exactly why customers must slow down. No bank in Nigeria will ask you to confirm your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link,” Sipe said. Sipe acknowledged the efforts of banks to strengthen fraud detection and customer protection, alongside regulatory measures introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s mandatory cybersecurity self assessment guide. He stressed, however, that these efforts must be complemented by customer awareness and vigilance, particularly when handling requests for sensitive banking information. “Banks can strengthen their security systems, but fraudsters continue to find ways to exploit unsuspecting customers. We must all remain vigilant. Always pause, verify requests through official channels and report anything suspicious before taking action,” he added. Sipe urged customers to avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages asking them to verify, reactivate or secure their bank accounts. He also warned against sharing personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), card verification values (CVVs) or BVNs in response to suspicious requests. Customers should verify such requests directly with their banks through official mobile applications, verified social media accounts or published customer service numbers. nigeria.title: World Ports Confab: FG woos global investors with maritime reforms
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has intensified efforts to attract global investment into Nigeria’s maritime sector by showcasing the Federal Government’s ongoing port reforms and investor-friendly policies at the World Ports Conference, highlighting opportunities for private sector participation, improved port efficiency and sustainable growth. Speaking at the ongoing World Ports Conference in London, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, showcased President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s maritime policies and its positioning of Nigeria’s Ports as Africa’s biggest economy that is yearning for global investment. He affirmed that the speed of growth and development in the country’s ports signifies the huge opportunities investors should tap into, adding that the current administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has put policies in place that are investment friendly. The NPA boss identified Nigeria’s huge population, urbanization, and infrastructural gaps in the ports as attractive opportunities for investment in its maritime and associated sectors. Dantsoho, who is also the Vice- President of the International Association of Ports & Harbours (IAPH) and doubles as Chairman of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA) told investors that Africa’s untapped resources remain the best destination for ports investment and development. He said the government alone cannot fund development of bigger or deeper sea ports and other similar projects hence the need for investors to take advantage of such opportunities across the continent. Dantsoho affirmed that “Nigeria has the highest population in Africa. So, the speed of growth is something that really should concern us. For example, in Nigeria, only recently, about 3 years ago, we commissioned the first deep sea port in Nigeria, which is called Lekki Deep Sea Port, that was funded by the Chinese government in relationship with China Harbor, and the expenditure cost us $1.6 billion to build Lekki in Lagos. nigeria.title: BoI advocates investment in industrial clusters to boost Lagos economy
nigeria.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Bank of Industry (BOI) has called for increased investment in industrial clusters, reliable power supply and supporting infrastructure to boost productivity, attract private capital and strengthen the Lagos State economy. Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, BoI, Dr. Olasupo Olusi made this call in a keynote address delivered at the 4th edition of the Lagos Economic Outlook 2027 Discourse, themed, ‘“Development Pathways, Emerging Risks and Strategic Policy Priorities.’ Represented by Dr. Isa Omagu, General Manager, MD/CEO’s Office, BoI, Olusi said investment in industrial clusters, particularly along major industrial and port corridors, would help businesses overcome production constraints, reduce operating costs and improve their competitiveness. He also said Lagos must assess economic progress by the improvements businesses and residents experience, rather than relying solely on economic growth figures and public spending. “The test is whether Lagos becomes more productive and more liveable,” he said. He identified electricity costs, traffic congestion, access to appropriate financing and institutional coordination as major constraints to business productivity. “A manufacturer needs reliable electricity. A worker needs a commute that does not consume productive hours. Firms need predictable approvals, appropriate finance and customers,” he said. Olusi urged the state to prioritise investment in power infrastructure serving industrial clusters, faster freight movement, streamlined business approvals, flood-resilient commercial routes and skills development. Speaking at the event, Lagos State Commissioner for Economic Planning and Budget, Mr. Ope George, said the ministry would continue to coordinate economic intelligence, development planning, budget management and performance monitoring in support of Lagos State’s long-term development aspirations. He said the 2027 economic outlook provided an opportunity to consolidate the state’s achievements, address structural challenges and strengthen its position as a competitive and resilient economy. “Our focus goes beyond economic projections. It is about shaping policies that will strengthen competitiveness, promote inclusive growth and secure a sustainable future for Lagos State,” George said. Earlier, Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget, Mrs. Olayinka Ojo, highlighted the state’s development planning, budget monitoring and performance evaluation frameworks. She said Lagos was strengthening evidence-based governance through its long-term development plan, Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, annual budgets and regular monitoring of revenue, expenditure and project delivery. Ojo also highlighted the government’s engagement with communities and the use of platforms to improve citizens’ access to information on public projects and social intervention programmes. nigeria.title: Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years
nigeria.description: •Cargoes to ease pressure on substations, strengthen national grid — Tegbe By Udeme Akpan The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has released 98 containers of electricity transmission equipment stranded at the nation’s ports, some for up to 20 years, in a move expected to strengthen the national grid and improve electricity supply across the country. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this in Lagos, stating that 44 containers were released from ENL Terminal, while another 54 were cleared from APMT and Sun & Moon Terminals. He said the 98 containers represented part of more than 300 containers of transmission equipment held at the ports. The equipment, comprising high-capacity transformers, cables and switchgear, was procured to expand the transmission network, address overloaded substations and improve electricity delivery nationwide. Tegbe said: “The equipment was procured to expand the transmission network and relieve overloaded substations. Its detention stalled projects, kept existing substations under heavy strain, exposed valuable assets to deterioration and accumulated charges on the cargoes.” He noted that the prolonged detention of the equipment had imposed additional costs on businesses, households and public institutions, which continued to grapple with unreliable electricity supply. Also speaking, the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adeniyi, said the Service had commenced processes to clear the containers in collaboration with the Ministry of Power, the Nigerian Ports Authority and terminal operators. He said: “The release follows the President’s directive for immediate clearance and for agencies to resolve outstanding charges and administrative bottlenecks without delay.” Adeniyi pledged to work with the Minister until all the containers were cleared, while appealing to terminal operators to support the national effort. The Minister disclosed that an inspection of the recovered equipment showed that most of the items remained useful and viable. He said: “When evacuated, it will be verified, tested and refurbished where necessary, then deployed to project sites to complete stalled installations, relieve overloaded substations and strengthen constrained transmission corridors.” The post Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: COP31 Opens As Climate, Geopolitical Pressures Mount
nigeria.description: The UN’s annual climate talks kick off Monday in Turkey as rising temperatures heighten the urgency of action, with financial constraints and geopolitical tensions complicating efforts to secure global cooperation. More than 100,000 people are expected to attend COP31 in a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean seaside city of Antalya over the next two weeks. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are facing tough discussions over how to accelerate the energy transition and provide funds to help developing nations cope with the worsening climate emergency. But observers say few major breakthroughs are expected as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The climate emergency, meanwhile, continued to wreak havoc this year as punishing heatwaves baked Europe, wildfires raged in Indonesia, and a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods in Nepal. An exceptionally strong El Niño climate phenomenon is forecast to peak later this year, adding to extreme weather and possibly helping to make 2026 or 2027 the hottest year on record. The outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above preindustrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. “Global leaders must pull us back from the brink and commit to rapidly transitioning away from fossil fuels and expanding renewable energy, an imperative reinforced by the current energy affordability crisis,” said Rachel Cleetus, climate programme director at the Union of Concerned Scientists. A woman walks inside the COP31 venue at the Antalya Expo Center on November 8, 2026, ahead of the opening of the UN climate conference. ‘Clean’ Electrification? Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference. The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements. Turkey is promoting an “action agenda” alongside the formal negotiations that encourages countries to support non-binding pledges on issues from artificial intelligence to waste management. Its centrepiece is an “electrification” drive to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035. But the initiative could become a source of friction. The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of fossil fuels in the Turkish proposal. Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action. nigeria.title: 2026 Lagos Trade Fair: We’re poised to turn stability into prosperity — Tinubu
nigeria.description: By Yinka Kolawole President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria’s next economic priority is to translate the gains of ongoing reforms into prosperity through enterprise, industrial growth and expanded trade. Tinubu spoke at the weekend, at the opening of the 40th Lagos International Trade Fair, organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), at Tafawa Balewa Square, Lagos. The president, represented by the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, said the Federal Government had made significant progress in stabilising the economy, adding that the focus must now shift to stimulating production, creating jobs and expanding business opportunities. “The emergency is over. The foundation has been repaired. Our task now is to turn stability into prosperity, and enterprise is at the heart of that task,” he said. Highlighting the administration’s economic achievements, Tinubu said Nigeria’s gross external reserves rose to approximately $55.07 billion in October 2026, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves exceeded $40 billion, from less than $4 billion in 2023. He also noted that inflation declined to 14.63 per cent in September 2026, while the economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, describing the figures as evidence of improving economic fundamentals. nigeria.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan A quiet transformation is reshaping how branded food items and cooking oils move from distribution warehouses to neighborhood shops, across major wholesale food markets in Nigeria. Read Also: Can 142m Nigerian youths change 2027 elections narrative? Faced with persistent inflation, tight liquidity, and shrinking consumer purchasing power, Economy&Lifestyle findings show that bulk food warehouses are increasingly breaking down standard 50-kilogram sacks and full cartons into half-measures for small-scale retailers. Traditionally, wholesale depots in major distribution centers across the country operated on strict minimum-order volumes. Retailers were required to purchase full 50kg bags of rice, beans, or garri, full cartons of noodles, or 25-liter kegs of vegetable oil. However, as wholesale prices are consistently rising over the past two years, many corner-shop owners and market stall traders are finding it difficult to raise the capital needed to restock full units across multiple product lines. In response, warehouse operators and major distributors have adapted their inventory models, introducing official ‘half-bag’ and ‘split-carton’ wholesale tiers. Instead of turning away undercapitalised buyers, depot managers now employ dedicated staff to weigh, re-bag, and seal 25kg portions of grains and split bulk cartons of packaged foods at wholesale rates. Alhaji Musa Danjuma, a bulk grain distributor, said: “If we insist on selling only full bags, our goods will sit in the warehouse until they spoil or expire. “A retailer, who used to buy 10 full bags of local parboiled rice can barely afford three today. “By splitting bags into halves and quarters at wholesale margins, we keep our stock moving and help small traders keep their shelves stocked.” The shift has provided immediate relief for micro-retailers who form the backbone of Nigeria’s informal food distribution network. For traders operating on thin daily margins, tying up scarce capital in a single full sack of beans or sugar often meant leaving customers without other essentials like pasta, seasoning cubes, or vegetable oil. “Before now, buying one full bag of brown beans took almost all my weekly capital,” said Mrs. Ngozi Okafor, a provision store owner. “Now, the warehouse allows me to pick half a bag of beans, half a bag of rice, and half a carton of spaghetti. “My shop looks full again, and my customers do not have to walk away empty-handed because I ran out of one items.” Market analysts note that while this fractional wholesale model keeps supply chains active, it introduces minor operational costs for warehouses, including extra packaging materials, labor for re-weighing, and heightened vigilance against weight discrepancies. nigeria.description: By Jide Ajani There is perhaps no greater threat to electoral integrity than an unreliable Voters’ Register. Before the first ballot is cast or the first result announced, the credibility of an election is already being determined by the document that establishes who is entitled to vote. Read Also: * Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal The Voters’ Register is the foundation of the electoral process. It defines the electorate, determines the numerical strength of constituencies and provides the basis for accreditation and voting. It is, fundamentally, the official record of a people’s democratic membership. Yet, in Nigeria, its credibility remains a persistent source of anxiety. The historical paradox: have we really progressed? Nigeria has travelled a considerable distance from the largely manual registration arrangements of the 1950s to biometric registration, electronic databases and the deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). The 1959 general election, conducted under the Electoral Commission of Nigeria (ECN), had approximately nine million registered voters. Subsequent elections in 1964/65, 1979, 1983 and 1993 exposed different administrative and political challenges associated with voter registration. 4th Republic The Fourth Republic introduced more sophisticated systems, including permanent voter cards, biometric identification and mechanisms for detecting duplicate registrations. Yet technological advancement has not necessarily translated into greater electoral credibility. A bigger register is not automatically a better register. A digital register is not necessarily reliable, and biometric technology is not beyond manipulation. Consider the fluctuations in registration figures: 73.5 million in 2011, 67.4 million in 2015 and approximately 84 million in 2019. Constitutional independence in itself does not guarantee operational independence when the personnel saddled with responsibilities decide to go rogue on the system. When public confidence in INEC declines, virtually every administrative decision becomes vulnerable to suspicion, from voter registration and PVC distribution to accreditation and results management. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. sports.title: 'I'm so tired and also disappointed' - Matheus Cunha admits sitting in the relegation zone 'is not normal' after Manchester United's 4-4 thriller against Aston Villa
sports.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United forward Matheus Cunha has expressed his exhaustion and frustration after his side twice fought back from two goals down to salvage a 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa. Despite rescuing a dramatic late point at Old Trafford on Sunday, the Red Devils enter the November international break languishing in 18th place. Brazilian forward laments slow starts Cunha played the full 90 minutes on Sunday after inspiring a midweek 3-2 Champions League comeback win over Roma , earning a 16th-minute penalty when fouled by Boubacar Kamara and testing keeper Zion Suzuki from distance. Bruno Fernandes converted that spot-kick before Youri Tielemans cancelled out early strikes from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson. After John McGinn's penalty and Leon Goretzka made it 4-2, stoppage-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point . Late comebacks mask mentality issue Questioning why his team only show urgency after falling behind, Cunha told Sky Sports : "I'm so tired and also disappointed. After the other night [against Roma] we talked about how we concede goals and have the mentality to come back in the game. "We did it again where we had to play like Manchester United and go forward. We showed courage, but we only do this after we concede goals. "We showed character after conceding goals. If we had shown that character and courage before, then we will win more games. "I don't know why we are making it hard for ourselves. We all work hard, and we all want to be the best. We need to change our mentality from the beginning." Attacker sympathises with frustrated supporters Failing to keep a clean sheet across their opening 10 league games for the first time since 1986-87 has left United in their lowest position at this stage of a top-flight campaign since sitting 20th that same season. Understanding why the Old Trafford faithful are unhappy , Cunha added: "Before we played, everyone is a fan. You understand why they are frustrated. This is completely fine; we understand. "We are on the pitch, and we need to manage this. We need to change the mentality, be in the game. I don't think the fans are against us; it's just that they want to see us perform and win games. "Before anything else, we need to look inside to us - the players, the staff. It's a huge club and to feel something like this [being so low down in the standings] is not normal." Liverpool test awaits after hiatus Winless in eight Premier League outings to match a barren run from April to May 2025, United are now guaranteed to spend at least 15 straight days in the drop zone , their longest top-flight stretch since a 28-day spell in September and October 1986. Cunha and his team-mates must use the two-week international pause to fix their defensive flaws. Once domestic action resumes in a fortnight, the Red Devils face a daunting clash against rivals Liverpool.

sports.title: MVPW07 Results: Baumgardner Defuses Turhan, Unification Fight Looming
sports.description: What to Know Women’s boxing thrilled fans in Arlington, Texas and watching on ESPN at Most Valuable Promotions’ MVPW07 card on Sunday. Alycia Baumgardner took Elif Nur Turhan to the cleaners with three shutout scorecards in a dominating performance. Ramla Ali scored her biggest, while Irma Garcia and Skye Nicolson defended their titles. In Sunday’s main event on the Most Valuable Promotions MVPW07 card, Alycia Baumgardner of Detroit stepped up and showed out in her first fight as a lightweight. Alycia Baumgardner reacts to her three shutout scorecards declaring her the winner. Photo: Most Valuable Promotions “The Bomb” thoroughly defused one of boxing’s hard-punching women and our 2025 Fighter of the Year , Elif Nur Turhan of Turkey. Turhan did not win a single round on any of the three scorecards against Baumgardner, a triple 100-90 shutout. Baumgardner is now the IBF World Lightweight champion. It was the first loss for “The Golden Turkish Warrior” Turhan (14-1, 8 KOs) at the hands of Baumgardner (19-1, 7 KOs ), who has never looked more in control. “This was somebody that I was very humble to fight, and I needed this fight to keep me humble, to keep me hungry, and be the best fighter that I can be,” said Baumgardner. Baumgardner and trainer Derrick James trained hard and put together the ideal game plan against Turhan. Turhan swings for the fences, relying on her power much like a male heavyweight who can lose every round but win the fight with a single punch. They recognized that Baumgardner could neutralize her with speed, with a stinging jab and straight power shots. Baumgardner said she and James knew Turhan would come out swinging. “ We knew that’s how she comes to fight. So it was all about staying composed and staying true to what I’m great at, and that’s keeping my hands up. That’s being skillful. The skills pay the bills, baby!” Baumgardner landed more than half of her power punches thanks to her superior accuracy and counterpunching. She was well conditioned to fight three-minute rounds, saying she sparred more than 160 rounds in training camp. It paid off: her punch output increased through the fight, and she threw and landed the most punches in the final round as Turhan faded. According to CompuBox, Turhan landed an average of just five punches per round. Baumgardner landed 43% of her punches thrown in combination to just 16% for Turhan. “I was prepared for that fight, and so when I’m in there, I just think, man, I trained for this,” said Baumgardner. “This was supposed to be the fun part, and I definitely made it fun and made it exciting and entertaining, and I hope everybody was entertained tonight.” Sitting ringside watching with great interest was WBC/WBO World Lightweight champion Caroline Dubois, who will face WBA World Lightweight champion Stephanie Han to unify the rest of the titles on February 20 in El Paso . Count on a fight for undisputed between the winner and Baumgardner in the spring. Ramla Ali Wins First World Title

sports.title: Footballer to help kids get their kicks outdoor
sports.description: Hull City captain Lewie Coyle is encouraging children to play with a smile [Jasmine Lowe/BBC News] The captain of a Premier League team has launched a street football programme to encourage more children to enjoy outdoor play. Hull City defender Lewie Coyle said his career began by kicking a ball in an alleyway near the East Hull home where he grew up and he has called for more children to follow in his footsteps. The 31-year-old said: "I believe being allowed to lark (play) about outside gave me a head start in pursuing what my career has turned out to be as a professional footballer." Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, is backing Coyle's call: "Playing outside develops confidence, creativity, resilience and independence. It's good for physical and mental health." Coyle led his hometown club to victory in the Championship play-off final in May, securing the Tigers' promotion to the Premier League. Through the Lewie Coyle Football Academy, the defender is launching LCFA Street Football and has vowed to visit estates across the city and hold free pop-up events to encourage outdoor play among children. Coyle said his Hull City team-mates had donated as part of the campaign to ensure every child taking part received a free football. He said: "I just want to encourage kids to move again. We need kids to be kids and play on the street, but of course, in a safe environment. "I had so many amazing memories growing up on the streets of Bilton. It taught me confidence and social skills, and it was character-building. "We're in an era now where kids socialise through technology, but I think as adults we need to make sure there's more of a push for our children to play out in the same way we did. "We're going to chuck some jumpers down and use them as goalposts, and we're really going to throw it back. As it says on the tin, we're just going to have a kickabout on the streets." Scunthorpe-born Dame Rachel de Souza is backing Lewie Coyle's call for more outdoor play [PA Media] Coyle's message has been backed by de Souza, who said it echoed new research from her office that showed "boys and girls want to play outside". She said: "I've spoken to children across the nation through my Big Future survey and, from Land's End to Hadrian's Wall, I hear the same message: boys and girls want to play. "They want to be outside, be active and be with friends in places where they feel safe and welcome. "But, there are so many barriers right now, from the cost of living to a lack of places to go, especially for teenagers and disabled children. "We all need to champion play and remember that childhood can't be, and shouldn't be, completely risk-free." sports.title: OTD (09/11/1992): Crosby Is Caretaker At Sunderland… Again!
sports.description: Sunderland 1-2 Leicester, League match at Roker Park, Sunday 15th November 1992. Brian Atkinson, Sunderland, gets the better of Colin Hull of Leicester. (Photo by NCJ Archive/Mirrorpix/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just six months earlier, it was probably the proudest moment in Malcolm Crosby’s footballing career as he led Sunderland out at Wembley as the manager who had taken them to the final and was ninety minutes away from becoming immortal. It wasn’t to be, as Liverpool ran out comfortable winners on the day, but then the real work was to begin. First up, his captain Paul Bracewell was fobbed off by the Sunderland board, so joined Keegan’s revolution up the road. Then Paul Hardyman had a tantrum because he was left out of the FA Cup final squad and joined Bristol Rovers. It was compounded by the fact that, after a whole host of players were linked with joining the club, only three signed to join the ranks. Shaun Cunnington from Grimsby Town, John Colquhoun from Hearts and, at weekends, Crosby’s assistant Bobby Ferguson called up his mate Terry Butcher to help us out, as his knee wouldn’t allow him to train. Things weren’t looking good to begin with, but four wins in the first 14 games confirmed everyone’s fears. It would be another season of struggle in Barclays League Division One (the Championship in new money). Two days earlier, Crosby’s Sunderland had been demolished 5-2 at Chris Turner’s Peterborough United, with the home side being 4-1 up on the hour mark. With the form the way it was, the table was looking bleak and, after a capitulation at London Road, it was looking like the end for Crosby as Sunderland manager. However, two days later, it was reported by Geoff Storey in the Sunderland Echo that Crosby would indeed be in the dugout for the next fixture at Roker Park against Leicester City. This wasn’t because the Roker boss had received a vote of confidence. It was reported “that the board had not been able to come up with a replacement that would appease disgruntled fans”. This led to comments by Aidan Semmens in the Echo, stating: “Malcolm Crosby began his career as Sunderland manager as caretaker. Now it seems he is in a caretaker’s role again”. There had been no word from chairman Bob Murray or the directors on the manager’s position, so much so that publicly Crosby believed his job was not under immediate threat: Everybody keeps going on about it, saying the board will sack me. The board has been great. They have let me get on with the job, but unfortunately we haven’t backed it up with results. Whatever decisions people make I, as a manager, have got to accept that decision. If they say enough is enough, I will have to accept that. Everybody knows that when you become a manager. I’m not worried about being sacked. What worries me is how we can play well in the two previous matches and at times play well against Peterborough, but then let goals in like we have. I’m worried about the players and I’m concerned for the supporters.

sports.title: Lakers hold off Pistons behind Austin Reaves’ 43 with Luka Dončić out
sports.description: Nov 8, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves (15) passes the ball from under the basket against the Detroit Pistons in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. DETROIT — The Lakers had led by 26. By the fourth quarter, that lead was down to one, and the NBA’s leading scorer was on the bench in street clothes. Austin Reaves took it from there. He hit an off-balance 3-pointer with 46 seconds left, waved toward the courtside seats and closed out a season-high 43-point night at the free-throw line as the Lakers beat the Detroit Pistons 121-116 on Sunday at Little Caesars Arena. The Lakers improved to 9-2 with their fifth straight win and are 2-0 without Luka Dončić, who missed his second game of the season with lower back tightness. Reaves went 14 of 27 from the field, made four of six 3-pointers and hit all 11 free throws. He added five rebounds and four assists and committed just one turnover against the NBA’s top-ranked defense. “I thought AR’s decision-making, his aggression, his ability to just consistently touch the paint and get downhill was fantastic tonight,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Quentin Grimes scored 10 of his 12 points in the first quarter, when L.A. shot 16 of 23 and built a 38-14 lead. The Lakers stretched it to 40-14 early in the second before Detroit’s bench brought the Pistons back. Daniss Jenkins scored 22 of his career-high 31 points in the first half, including a 3-pointer at the buzzer that cut the deficit to 61-48. Reaves scored 13 in the third quarter, but Detroit closed within three late in the period. The Pistons had a chance to tie it with 9:14 left in the fourth, when Cade Cunningham missed the second of two free throws to leave L.A. ahead 90-89. “We just stayed calm,” Reaves told Spectrum SportsNet. “You can get sped up in those types of moments, but we trust what we got on this team.” Walker Kessler helped rebuild the lead with a huge putback and a free throw to give L.A. an eight point lead with 2:15 left. He finished with 12 points, 16 rebounds and three blocks, while Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams each scored 17 off the bench. Kevin Huerter added 24 for Detroit, and Cunningham finished with 14 points and eight assists. The Lakers visit the Atlanta Hawks on Monday to close out the back-to-back.

technology.title: Linus Torvalds sees signs AI-prompted patch flood has peaked
technology.description: The worst of the patchpocalypse may be behind us, according to Linus Torvalds. Writing in his weekly kernel update post , the Linux kernel dev leader delivered Linux 7.4 rc2 – the second rough cut of the next kernel – which he rated as a big release for two reasons. One is that he left some code out of rc1, because he was busy and because it was already the largest such release in the history of the kernel. The other is what Torvalds described as “various AI fixes.” Such fixes are necessary because ever since Anthropic launched its Mythos bug-finding model in April , developers have been able to find more software flaws than was previously possible. Microsoft, for example, addressed a record 974 flaws in September – its third record fixing spree this year after it whacked 622 flaws in July and 206 in June. Oracle addressed 1,449 flaws in a single month. That’s many more patches than IT teams are set up to handle, yet they must find ways to deal with bugs more quickly because attackers are increasingly targeting flaws found by AI . Torvalds’ post suggests that, perhaps, the worst of this is behind us. “This time around Alexei claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true,” he wrote. That’s a reference to Alexei Starovoitov, co-creator and lead dev on the Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF), the project that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs within the Linux kernel. “I think most other areas haven't reached that point yet, but it's at least a sign that we _may_ be starting to see the tide starting to turn,” he added. “Don't hold your breath, but maybe cross your fingers we'll be getting there in the not entirely distant future.” If Torvalds is correct, that’s welcome news. The Linux kernel’s 40-million-plus lines of code makes it one of the world’s bigger software projects. If AI soon stops finding flaws in other parts of the kernel beyond eBPF, perhaps the deluge of fixes developers and users alike will need to handle has peaked. ®

China’s government is an enormous buyer, and losing the chance to bid for its business is unlikely to be helpful. Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch? The nebula is known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula because, it is said, the nebula’s shape resembles a Halloween-style caricature of a witch’s head. Exactly how, though, can be a topic of imaginative speculation . What is clear is that IC 2118 is about 50 light-years across and made of gas and dust that points to — because it has been partly eroded by — the nearby star Rigel . One of the brighter stars in the constellation Orion, Rigel lies just below the center of the featured image . The blue color of the Witch Head Nebula and is caused not only by Rigel’s intense blue starlight but also because the dust grains scatter blue light more efficiently than red. The same physical process causes Earth’s daytime sky to appear blue , although the scatterers in planet Earth’s atmosphere are molecules of nitrogen and oxygen . NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin This story is an update to the Antarctic ozone hole feature in our World of Change series , which documents how Earth changes over months, seasons, and years. The stratospheric ozone layer protects life on Earth by absorbing ultraviolet light, which damages DNA in plants and animals (including humans) and leads to sunburns and skin cancer. Prior to 1979, scientists had not observed atmospheric ozone concentrations below 220 Dobson Units . But in 1985, British Antarctic Survey scientists using ground-based measurements at Halley Research Station reported that Earth’s natural sunscreen was thinning dramatically over Antarctica each spring. NASA satellite instruments revealed the continental scale of this Antarctic ozone thinning, and it came to be known as the ozone hole. The data visualizations below shows the ozone hole each year from 1979 through 2026 (no data are available for 1995). The measurements were made from 1979-2004 by the TOMS (NASA’s Total Ozone Mapping Spectrometer) instruments on Nimbus-7 and several additional satellites; from 2005-2011 by the OMI (Ozone Monitoring Instrument) on the Aura satellite; from 2012-2025 by the OMPS (Ozone Mapping and Profiler Suite) on the Suomi NPP satellite; and in 2026 by the OMPS on the NOAA-20 satellite. Red and yellow areas indicate the ozone hole. As the images show, the word hole isn’t literal; no place is empty of ozone. Scientists use the word hole as a metaphor for the area in which ozone concentrations drop below the historical threshold of 220 Dobson Units . Using this metaphor, they can describe the hole’s area and depth.
